target.title: fix(memory-host-sdk): prevent mid-transcript [cron:...] from wiping archive content
target.body:
<!--
Closes #98241
Related PR: #98246 (same root cause, similar approach)
-->

## Summary

**Problem**: Mid-transcript `[cron:...]` text (pasted log lines, user-typed `[cron:` prefix) silently wipes all prior archive content from `memory_search`. The content-based cron heuristic (`isGeneratedCronPromptMessage`) matches ANY user message that starts with `[cron:...]`, setting `generatedByCronRun = true` and clearing accumulated content.

**Solution**: Remove the content-based cron heuristic entirely. The record-level provenance check (`isCronRunGeneratedRecord`, which inspects each JSONL record's `sessionKey` field) handles all genuine cron archives — records retain their cron-run session keys even after session reset/delete.

**What changed**: Deleted the `isGeneratedCronPromptMessage` content heuristic and its `!sessionStoreAlreadyClassifiedCron` / `!hasSeenPriorUserMessage` guards from `buildSessionEntry`. Net -13 lines.

**What did NOT change**: The `isCronRunGeneratedRecord` record-level provenance check is preserved. `sanitizeSessionText` still strips `[cron:...]` messages from rendered content (cosmetic, doesn't affect other messages). All existing cron archive behavior is unchanged for archives with record-level provenance or session store classification.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes silent data loss: users who paste cron log output or type `[cron:` mid-conversation lose all earlier archive history from `memory_search`. The old content-based heuristic matched ANY user message text starting with `[cron:...]`, not just genuine cron-run records. This affected session archive processing in `buildSessionEntry` during gateway memory sync.

## Root Cause

The content-based heuristic `isGeneratedCronPromptMessage` was a duplicate signal — `isCronRunGeneratedRecord` (checking each record's `sessionKey` for cron-run patterns) already classified all genuine cron archives correctly. The text-pattern match was redundant and only caused false positives for human-authored `[cron:...]` content without corresponding record-level provenance.

## Evidence

### 1. Unit test suite (39 tests, all pass)

```bash
pnpm test packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/session-files.test.ts
```

```text
 ✓ |unit-fast| session-files.test.ts > buildSessionEntry > indexes usage-counted reset/deleted archives
 ✓ |unit-fast| session-files.test.ts > buildSessionEntry > keeps cron-run deleted archives opaque
 ✓ |unit-fast| session-files.test.ts > buildSessionEntry > keeps cron-run reset archives opaque
 ✓ |unit-fast| session-files.test.ts > buildSessionEntry > does not wipe archive content when [cron:...] appears mid-transcript
 ✓ |unit-fast| session-files.test.ts > buildSessionEntry > does not treat first-turn [cron:...] as cron when records lack cron provenance
 ✓ |unit-fast| session-files.test.ts > buildSessionEntry > strips inbound metadata
 ✓ |unit-fast| session-files.test.ts > buildSessionEntry > skips inter-session user messages

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  39 passed (39)
```

### 2. Multi-scenario verification (production code path)

The `buildSessionEntry` function was called with realistic archive data covering all relevant edge cases. This is the exact same function the gateway calls during memory sync — no mocks, no stubs, built from the same TypeScript source compiled into the gateway dist.

**Real environment**: Linux 4.19.112 (x86_64), Node 24.13.1, OpenClaw dev checkout

```text
MID-TRANSCRIPT: [cron:...] after prior user msg does NOT wipe (THE FIX)
  [mid-transcript] contentLen=93 generatedByCronRun=undefined
  [mid-transcript] hasFirstMsg=true
  [mid-transcript] hasLastMsg=true
ORPHAN CRON: genuine cron archive stays opaque (no regression)
  [orphan-cron] generatedByCronRun=true
SESSION-STORE-CRON: store says cron stays opaque
NORMAL: no cron text content preserved
SESSION-STORE-NOT-CRON: not-cron store not wiped

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  5 passed (5)
```

| # | Scenario | Expected | Result |
|---|----------|----------|--------|
| 1 | Mid-transcript `[cron:...]` after prior user message | Content preserved, NOT marked cron | ✅ |
| 2 | Genuine orphan cron archive (records have cron-run session keys) | Opaque (marked cron) | ✅ |
| 3 | Session store says cron | Opaque via session-store classification | ✅ |
| 4 | Normal session, no cron text | Content fully preserved | ✅ |
| 5 | Session store says not-cron | Not wiped | ✅ |

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed**: Remove content-based cron heuristic that falsely classified human `[cron:...]` text as cron-generated, wiping archive content.

**Real environment tested**: Linux 4.19.112 (x86_64), Node 24.13.1, OpenClaw dev checkout (same `buildSessionEntry` code path the gateway uses during memory sync)

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
```bash
cd packages/memory-host-sdk
npx tsx src/host/proof-demo.ts
```

**After-fix evidence**:
```text
MID-TRANSCRIPT: [cron:...] after prior user msg does NOT wipe
  [mid-transcript] contentLen=93 generatedByCronRun=undefined
  [mid-transcript] hasFirstMsg=true
  [mid-transcript] hasLastMsg=true
Content preserved correctly.

ORPHAN CRON: genuine cron archive stays opaque (no regression)
  [orphan-cron] generatedByCronRun=true
Records retain cron-run session keys after reset/delete.

FIRST-TURN: human [cron:...] without record-level provenance
  Not classified as cron (generatedByCronRun=undefined)
  Content preserved (sanitized text but no cross-message wipe)
```

**Observed result after the fix**: Mid-transcript `[cron:...]` no longer wipes archive content. First-turn human `[cron:...]` without record-level provenance is no longer falsely classified as cron. Genuine orphan cron archives (with cron-run session keys in records) remain correctly opaque.

**What was not tested**: No real-world integration test against a running Gateway with live memory sync. The `buildSessionEntry` function is tested in isolation using realistic archive data matching the production JSONL format.

## Risk checklist

- **merge-risk: low** — removes a heuristic that caused false positives; record-level provenance is the correct discriminator
- **Risk mitigation**: Added test coverage for mid-transcript and first-turn `[cron:...]` scenarios. All 39 existing tests pass. Genuine cron archives confirmed opaque via record-level `isCronRunGeneratedRecord` check.
- **Backwards compatible**: Yes for all archives with record-level cron provenance (records retain session keys after reset/delete). Archives without provenance that were previously falsely classified as cron will now be searchable — this is the correct behavior.
- **Regression risk**: Low — genuine cron archives are identified through record-level `isCronRunGeneratedRecord` checks, which are preserved. `sanitizeSessionText` still strips `[cron:...]` content from rendered output.

## Linked context

- **Issue**: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/98241 — mid-transcript `[cron:...]` archive content wipe
- **Related PR**: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/98246 — same root cause, approached via trusted provenance
- **Original change introducing heuristic**: Commit `2ffdb5d248` — added both `isCronRunGeneratedRecord` (record-level) and `isGeneratedCronPromptMessage` (content-based) signals alongside archive searchability
